newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC to revise up wheat carryover estimate.
newsitem.headline: ONIC to revise up wheat carryover estimate.

text.p: France's ONIC cereals office is poised to revise up its forecast for the amount of soft wheat carryover stock held at the end of this month, grain industry sources said on Monday.
Figures drafted for ONIC's next monthly grain report, due for publication on Wednesday, show carryover stocks of 2.268 million tonnes, compared with a previous estimate of 2.12 million tonnes.
Last year's June 30 carryover was 2.204 million tonnes.
ONIC routinely declines to comment on draft figures for its supply/demand report, which can be fine-tuned by ONIC members before release.
The industry sources confirmed that 1996/97 soft wheat exports to non-EU countries had been cut to 6.3 million tonnes in the draft version from 6.45 million the previous month.
But this was partly offset by a rise in exports within the European Union to a new record of 9.42 million tonnes.
The cut in non-EU exports is linked partly to delays in executing oil-for-food sales to Iraq, sources said on Friday.

In other changes, ONIC is expected to revise total supplies (after on-farm consumption) up slightly to 33 million tonnes, after an upward adjustment of some 150,000 tonnes in the 1996 delivered harvest to 30.660 million tonnes.
Demand on the internal market is seen likely to be revised up by about 50,000 tonnes to 12.632 million tonnes. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
